about: Every VENDOR CLAIM this repository asserts, pinned so it can be re-verified on a schedule instead of by a person remembering. STANDARD.md and several checks cite Claude Code and Codex behaviour as fact; before this file, each of those citations was a page someone read once and a date they wrote down. On 2026-08-15 that cost us a ratified ADR: ADR 0048 was accepted on the premise that a command is not a skill, which Claude Code's own documentation contradicts, and a 2026-08-10 internal audit had already found it. This file is the instrument that makes that failure mode detectable.

conventions.claim: The verbatim sentence, or the empirically observed behaviour, that this repository depends on. Never a paraphrase: a paraphrase cannot be checked against a page. A quote claim MUST be a COMPLETE SEMANTIC SENTENCE, not an identifier or a noun phrase. Review wave 2 found two claims pinned as bare tokens ('Plugin agents support', 'disable-model-invocation'): a page saying the field was REMOVED still contains the token, so the watch would report holds while the thing it guards had been deleted. tests/unit/vendor-watch.test.mjs now requires every quote claim to survive a MEANING REVERSAL that retains its distinctive tokens, so a new fragment cannot be added without the test noticing.
conventions.kind: quote = a sentence that MUST still appear on the named page; the watch checks it automatically. probe = an empirical behaviour that no page states, re-verified by running something; the watch can only report its AGE and name the reproduction, never confirm it.
conventions.dependsOn: What breaks, or becomes wrong, if this claim stops being true. This is the field that makes a failure actionable rather than interesting.
conventions.verifiedOn: ISO date a HUMAN last read this source in context. It is not the date the sentence was last machine-confirmed - the watch re-confirms every quote claim against the live page on every run, and is write-incapable, so it can never refresh this field. The two facts are different and were once conflated: for a QUOTE this date is advisory and a stale one is reported without blocking, because the watch checks the sentence and only a person checks whether the section around it still means the same thing. For a PROBE it is the whole verification, since no fetch can confirm the behaviour, so past the 30-day window it BLOCKS until someone re-runs the reproduction. Refresh it as a record of a reading, never to make a run green.
conventions.onChange: What a maintainer must do when this claim fails. Stated per claim because the answer differs: some changes are green-ward and are a silent re-read, others are a Standard revision needing an ADR and a migration window.
conventions.antecedent: OPTIONAL. Present only when the pinned sentence contains a pronoun or reference whose meaning is fixed by neighbouring text that is deliberately NOT pinned. It records what the reference points to and why the surrounding sentence was left out, so a reader is never asked to trust that a dangling 'one' means what the check assumes.

sources.note: The older docs.claude.com path 301-redirects here. A host move is a documentation edit, not a Standard revision.
Covers the commands-into-skills merge and the invocation-control frontmatter.
Subagent discovery: recursion, scoped identifiers, and the colon exclusion. Added 2026-08-15 after review wave 1 found U15 built on a flat-directory assumption nothing was watching.

claims.claim: For security reasons, hooks, mcpServers, and permissionMode are not supported for plugin-shipped agents
dependsOn: the marketplace A6 reading, which imports the same field list
claims.onChange: ASYMMETRIC (ADR 0045). A field REMOVED from the unsupported list is green-ward - update the constant, bump the read date, note it in CHANGELOG. A field ADDED is red-ward: a new Standard minor with finding-level migration metadata, never a bump of U14's own since.

claims.claim: Plugin agents support name, description, model, effort, maxTurns, tools, disallowedTools, skills, memory, background, and isolation frontmatter fields.
dependsOn: PLUGIN_AGENT_SUPPORTED_FIELDS, quoted in every U14 finding as the remediation
claims.onChange: Re-read the field list and update the constant. The list appears in user-facing remediation, so a stale one sends authors to a field the runtime does not accept.

claims.claim: Custom commands have been merged into skills
dependsOn: S7 (command-contract), which certifies a per-target command shape
claims.onChange: If this is ever REVERSED, sec 3.2's justification returns to component type and ADR 0048's amendment must be revisited. This claim is here because its absence was not noticed for five days after an internal audit found it.

claims.claim: Add disable-model-invocation: true to prevent Claude from triggering it automatically.
dependsOn: ADR 0048's corrected reasoning: a command is a skill whose invocation is user-controlled
backlog E44, which becomes an ADR when this field appears in a measured corpus
claims.onChange: If the field is renamed or removed, E44's trigger condition changes and ADR 0048's reasoning needs a new anchor.

claims.claim: Plugin agents/ directories are also scanned recursively
dependsOn: U15 (agents-dir-registerable) - its list-equality invariant is false if this changes
U14 (agent-restricted-fields), which reads the same runtime list
the S3 asymmetry, which relies on U15 owning every excluded file
claims.onChange: If discovery stops being recursive, the walk may flatten again - green-ward, a silent re-read. If the SCOPING rule changes, the name derivation must follow, because a nested agent's identity includes its subpath.

claims.claim: Claude Code doesn't load a file whose name contains one and logs an error to the debug log.
dependsOn: isRuntimeAgentFile in scripts/lib/fs-utils.mjs, which keeps both listers exactly as wide as the runtime
claims.antecedent: The 'one' is a colon, established by the preceding sentence: names can't contain ':', which is reserved for plugin-scoped identifiers. That sentence is not pinned because it carries a markdown link whose URL would fire on a docs reorganisation, which is noise rather than a change to the behaviour this repository depends on.
claims.onChange: If the runtime starts loading colon-named files, drop the exclusion: being stricter than the runtime is the opposite of the failure these listers prevent.

claims.claim: Claude Code scans agents/ for *.md and registers EVERY file it finds. A directory holding real-agent.md, README.md, _README.md and README.txt registered three subagents: real-agent, README and _README. The underscore prefix protects nothing; only the non-.md extension was skipped. NOTE: this probe covered a FLAT directory only. Recursion and the colon exclusion are separate QUOTE claims (agents-scanned-recursively, agent-filename-colon-excluded); generalising this probe past its evidence is what let nested agents bypass U14 and U15 until review wave 1.
dependsOn: U15 (agents-dir-registerable) - the whole check, and its vendor-cited provenance
the G8 exemption of agents/ from the meaningful-folder README requirement
claims.reproduction: Fixtures and step-by-step: docs/internal/vendor-watch/probes/agents-dir-registers-every-md/ (see EXPECTED.md for what each run observed, and probes/README.md for how to record the result). Install a plugin whose agents/ holds real-agent.md, README.md, _README.md and README.txt; list the registered subagents. Recorded in scripts/checks/folder-readme.mjs.
claims.onChange: If the runtime starts EXCLUDING README.md or underscore-prefixed files, U15 loses its vendor grounding and becomes a house convention - which would change its provenance, and with it whether plain-plugin drops it.

claims.claim: Component names from different plugins enter a SHARED POOL on any agent that does not namespace components by plugin, so two members shipping the same skill directory name collide and which one wins is undefined.
dependsOn: ADR 0051's stated reopening condition for marketplace-skill-collision and marketplace-command-collision
claims.reproduction: Fixtures and step-by-step: docs/internal/vendor-watch/probes/components-share-one-namespace/ (see EXPECTED.md for what each run observed, and probes/README.md for how to record the result). Install two plugins shipping the same skill name and observe which resolves.
claims.onChange: If a runtime NAMESPACES components by plugin, the two collision classes should be RETIRED, not graduated - ADR 0051 says so explicitly. This is the one claim whose change makes the gate report LESS, not more.
